answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is severe and non-negotiable. Renewing at current terms (memory_c1) will not meet the target. Switching vendors (memory_c2 showed sharp cuts) risks onboarding delays with zero buffer at 94% volume. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses risk but not cost urgently enough. Deferring is impossible—contract expires in 14 days. Negotiation is the only lever: memory_c4 demonstrated that benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and terms at renewal, and memory_c6 showed multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. Verify memory_c4 to confirm the benchmarking playbook and margin recovery magnitude. Verify memory_c2 to confirm the switching cost-cut was sustainable and what onboarding timeline looked like, to calibrate the real risk of switching if negotiation fails. The decision is to renegotiate hard, anchored to market rates, with a credible fallback to a tested low-cost vendor. This preserves uncertainty (negotiation outcome unknown, fallback unexercised) and flags downstream risk: if incumbent refuses to move sufficiently and we do switch, onboarding speed at 94% volume is a real hazard.
